title: The Hive Switch
frozenBasis: Official table of contents confirms chapter title and placement.
Official introduction supports the claim that morality can bind people into group-minded coordination.
Official Chapter 9 preview and surrounding book-level materials support the move toward explaining a shift from self to group.
supportablePoints: Chapter 10 likely explains the conditions under which people shift into more group-minded coordination.
The chapter probably treats the hive switch as an altered social mode rather than ordinary selfish calculation.
The chapter builds directly on Chapter 9's selfish-versus-groupish tension.
The chapter prepares the argument that religion can function as a team-binding technology.
unsupportedZones: No turning the hive switch into mystical certainty or unsupported neuro-detail.
No importing Chapter 11's religion claim as if Chapter 10 fully proves it already.
No flattening the chapter into generic crowd psychology.
